title: Tanzanian Andazi Buns
community: Universal morning street food — sold outside every school
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Street Maandazi — the classic Tanzanian fried dough sold outside every school, mosque, market, and bus stop. Slightly sweet, lightly cardamom-scented, crispy outside and soft within. The morning snack that Tanzania's children grow up with.
longDesc: Street maandazi is the morning food of Tanzania — sold in stacks by women who begin frying at 4am, bought by schoolchildren, workers, and commuters. The street version is made in large batches, cut and fried quickly, and sold warm. They are the everyday mandazi, unpretentious and beloved.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom, salt.
Beat egg into warm milk. Add melted butter.
Combine wet and dry ingredients. Mix to a soft dough.
Roll to 1cm. Cut into triangles or squares.
Fry at 170°C for 3—4 minutes per side until golden.
chefTips: The dough should be soft and slightly sticky.
Fresh is everything — buy at the pan, not after sitting.
cookingScience: See TZA007 for mandazi cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Made from simple, locally available ingredients.
culturalNote: Street maandazi are the food that Tanzania's schoolchildren have eaten outside the school gate for generations — bought with the few coins given for morning break, eaten hot, the sugar and cardamom the most comforting smell of childhood.
